problem: S3-CONC-01: `BackgroundTransferCoordinator.setPriority` checks the attach token, then awaits `driver.snapshot()`, then writes `priorities[name]` and awaits `driver.setPriority`. After the listing, D-9 re-checks the token and whether the task is still live. It never checks that this request is still the newest one for the name. Two overlapping changes from the engine therefore land in whatever order their listings finish. Example: a promotion when a user waiter joins a bulk background job, then a demotion when the waiter withdraws. The OS task and `liveTransfers()` end at 0.75 while the engine's lane is bulk (0.25), and they stay there until another change arrives. On top of that, `BackgroundTransferHandle` sends every control (setPriority, pause, cancel) through its own unstructured `Task`, so even their arrival order at the actor is not guaranteed. The engine-level R-NET-10 test cannot catch either problem: it runs over FakeRemoteSource, whose handle records synchronously. Scope: only when the app turns the background route on (ADR-026; bulk only, off by default).
fix: Background priority changes: the newest request wins (a per-name serial taken before the first `await` and checked after it, cleared on `.finished`), and a handle's controls are delivered in FIFO order (one stream per handle drained by one task, not a `Task` per call). Commit both probes (`concurrency/S3-CONC-01.swift` and `confirm-concurrency/S3-CONC-01-reverse.swift`) as regression tests; propose the D-9 ledger row amendment in the draft.

detail.fix: Make the newest request win inside the actor. Before the first await, bump a per-name request serial (`prioritySerial[name] += 1; let mine = ...`). After the listing, return unless `prioritySerial[name] == mine`, alongside the existing token and processed checks. Clear the serial in `process(.finished)`. Then deliver the handle's controls in order: feed them into one `AsyncStream` continuation per handle, drained by one task in FIFO order, instead of one `Task` per call. Without that, `setPriority(a); setPriority(b)` can still arrive as b then a. Add the probe as a regression test and amend ledger row D-9 to name the newest-request check.

confirmer.reason:
Reproduced against s3-base (09:53, load 33.4): `newestPriorityChangeWins` fails because the OS task ends at 0.75 (changes [0.25, 0.75]) and liveTransfers() disagrees with the newest request. I also wrote a confirmation for the direction that matters for H-4 (confirm-concurrency/S3-CONC-01-reverse.swift). An older demotion lands after a newer promotion, so the OS task ends at 0.25 (changes [0.75, 0.75, 0.25]) while a user is waiting.

I checked whether the interleaving can happen outside the fake. The hold seam is the same `holdNextSnapshot(.afterListing)` that the existing BackgroundInterleavingTests use, and in production three points can reorder controls:
(1) `BackgroundTransferHandle.setPriority/pause/cancel` (BackgroundSupport.swift:700-719) start one nonisolated `Task` per call on the global executor, so they can reach the actor in either order.
(2) `setPriority` (:422-441) awaits `driver.snapshot()`. The live driver does a holder-actor hop and `session.allTasks` off the actor, so a later request can finish its listing first. D-9 re-checks the token and processed set, but never whether this request is still the newest.
(3) `LiveBackgroundSessionDriver.setPriority` (BackgroundSessionBackend.swift:79) runs another `allTasks` and then `task.priority =` outside the coordinator, so two writes race there too.

The engine calls `handle.setPriority(lane)` synchronously on every lane change (EngineJobs.swift:197, EngineDispatch.swift:637-642) and never re-applies it later. A wrong value therefore stays until the next lane change.

Recorded decisions do not cover this. D-10 (adr-drafts/d.md) records the unstructured task per control but only weighs shutdown cancellation, not ordering. ADR-021 chose synchronous controls precisely so that controls stay ordered (S1-06), and this handle defeats that. ARCHITECTURE §7.5 says the priority is a hint, but that concerns what the OS does with the value. Here the library itself leaves the task at the value of an older lane, which breaks R-NET-10's MUST that engine priority maps to the URLSession task priority.

Scope: the route is off by default (ADR-026) and only carries key-free bulk work, so today's production configuration does not reach it.

Not refuted: the engine-level R-NET-10 test is not a G4 violation. It verifies the engine's ordering over FakeRemoteSource, as documented, but it does not cover the background coordinator.

The proposed fix is sound: a per-name request serial checked after the listing, plus one FIFO control stream per handle. Owner is WP-D (Sources/ZTronAssetTransport/**).

problem: S3-CONC-02: `handlers[identifier] = completionHandler` replaces a handler that has not been completed yet. Sequence: UIKit hands a second handler for the same session while the facade's first `handleBackgroundEvents` task is still waiting. The first task's `relay.complete(identifier)` then calls the second handler, which is early because its own events are not yet staged. The second task finds no handler. The first handler UIKit handed over is never called, although Apple requires every one to be called.
fix: `BackgroundEventsRelay.accept` (`BackgroundSupport.swift:733-750`) must never drop an uncompleted handler: every handler it accepts is called exactly once, and none before the events of its own wake are staged. Test both properties.

detail.requirements: R-NET-3 (SHOULD), REENTRANCY row RE-S42 ('the relay's completion runs once, after the events that preceded it were staged')
detail.problem: `handlers[identifier] = completionHandler` replaces a handler that has not been completed yet. Sequence: UIKit hands a second handler for the same session while the facade's first `handleBackgroundEvents` task is still waiting. The first task's `relay.complete(identifier)` then calls the second handler, which is early because its own events are not yet staged. The second task finds no handler. The first handler UIKit handed over is never called, although Apple requires every one to be called.
detail.evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/concurrency/S3-CONC-02.swift (test secondHandlerKeepsFirst), S3-CONC-02.log: `Expectation failed: calls.sorted() == ["first", "second"] ↳ each handler UIKit handed over runs once: ["second"]` (run 09:06, load avg 48.6)
detail.fix: Keep every accepted handler: `handlers: [String: [(ticket: UInt64, handler: () -> Void)]]`. `accept` returns or records a ticket. `complete(identifier:ticket:)` calls and removes the handlers accepted up to that ticket, since their preceding events were staged when the wait that began after them returned. Calling all pending handlers is also acceptable, because the latest wait covers the earlier ones. Never drop one uncalled. Update RE-S42's wording and keep the probe as a test.

confirmer.reason:
Reproduced (09:53): calls == ["second"], so the first handler is never called. `BackgroundEventsRelay.accept` (BackgroundSupport.swift:733-750) assigns `handlers[identifier] = completionHandler` and overwrites an uncompleted handler. `complete` removes and calls whatever is stored.

The coordinator side makes the early call real. One `.backgroundEventsFinished` runs `resumeFinishWaiters()` (BackgroundSupport.swift:579-584) and wakes both facade tasks (AssetClient.swift:435-454). The first task's `relay.complete` then calls the second handler, and the second task finds nothing.

No recorded decision covers this. The existing relay test only checks one handler completed once, and a fix that calls every pending handler keeps that test passing without a public API change.

Non-blocking because I could not prove the trigger. R-NET-3 is a SHOULD, and nothing shows that UIKit hands a second handler for the same session identifier while the first is still pending. That is device-only behaviour and goes under Not verified. It is not a Swift continuation or task leak, and no data is lost.

Owner is WP-D, since the relay lives in Transport. WP-G is only involved if the ticket variant changes `AssetClient.handleBackgroundEvents`.

detail.problem: Weak ETag accepted as the resume validator
detail.missing_test: SURVIVED. Missing test: loopback response with headers ETag: W/"v1" and Last-Modified (stall after half the body). detail.notes: The !tag.rawValue.hasPrefix("W/") check was removed, so resumeValidator returns .strongETag(W/...) and skips the Last-Modified fallback. A resumed request would then send a weak If-Range, which servers ignore, so the whole file is refetched. No test anywhere uses a weak ETag on the transport side. Survives Transport 151, Sync 351, Kit 85, Compat 71, Apple 104. Candidate: /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronAssetKit/.build-orchestrator/s3-probes/mut-network/M-N-22-candidate-test.swift.
